basis: Hand derivation from the specification text (csharpstandard, the pinned commit) of the 76 differential-oracle alternatives of the r2 expected asset, written without reading the expected types: for each alternative the acceptance of its witness source, the lexeme form and the extent of every instance of that form in the source, with a verbatim quote of the specification production. Each row states its comparison with the witness of the r2 asset (a span witness must have the extent of an instance, a starts-at witness the start of one; a row that names the terminals its node adds, with grammar grounds, compares the extent with those terminals) and the comparison of the witness before the after-native corrections (initial); the verifier recomputes both. The comparison covers the position of the witness only: it does not compare the types (ts) of these alternatives, and an instance list is what one reader derived from the text, not a parse.

rows.form: regular_interpolation: expression (',' interpolation_minimum_width)? Regular_Interpolation_Format? — between the braces, braces excluded
interpolation_minimum_width: constant_expression, after ',' (the sign belongs to the constant_expression: '-5' = unary minus + 5)
Interpolated_Regular_String_Start: the two characters $"
Interpolated_Regular_String_Mid: maximal run of Interpolated_Regular_String_Element between Start/{ … } and the next {/End; escapes ({{ }} \t \x41 \u0042) belong to it
Regular_Interpolation_Format: ':' Element+ — the colon belongs to the token; runs to the closing brace
Interpolated_Regular_String_End: the closing '"' (one char)
fragment alt 1/6 (a plain Character) is not a token of its own; it occurs inside Mid/Format tokens that contain >=1 non-escape character (S3 Mid has only escapes, so it is not an instance)

rows.form: argument_value: 'in' 'scoped'? variable_reference -> `in v` (keyword through the operand)
argument_value: 'ref' 'scoped'? variable_reference -> `ref v` (3 calls); `=> ref x` is a ref_method_body, not an argument
argument_value: 'out' 'scoped'? variable_reference | declaration expression -> `out var w`, `out int z`, `out _`
primary_expression: pointer_member_access (alt 27/30) -> `self->M`
unary_expression: pointer_indirection_expression (alt 11/12) -> `*p`
unary_expression: addressof_expression (alt 12/12) -> `&x`
type_parameter_constraints_clause: 'where' type_parameter ':' constraints — from `where` through the last constraint (9 clauses; `where` is a contextual keyword)
type_parameter_constraints: restrictive_type_parameter_constraints (alt 1/2) — the constraint list after ':' of each where clause
primary_constraint: 'class' nullable_type_annotation? — the keyword class right after `where T :`
primary_constraint: 'struct' — the keyword struct right after `where X :` (U of G, T of N)
constructor_constraint: 'new' '(' ')' — three tokens (the call Make<int, string>() is not one)
ref_kind: 'ref' (alt 1/2): the ref of `static ref int R` and of the ref parameters a and x of R; `ref readonly` of RR is alt 2/2; `=> ref x` is not a ref_kind
parameter_modifier: parameter_mode_modifier (alt 1/4): the keyword ref/out/in before the parameter type (five parameters)
parameter_mode_modifier: ref_kind (alt 1/3): ref on parameters (a, x of R)
parameter_mode_modifier: 'out' keyword on parameter b
parameter_mode_modifier: 'in' keyword on parameters c and x (RR)
pointer_type: dataptr_type (alt 1/3): value_type (*)+ or voidptr_type (*)+ — everything except bare void*
pointer_type: voidptr_type (alt 3/3): the two tokens void *
dataptr_type: value_type ('*')+ (alt 1/3): the value type name/keyword and all its stars
dataptr_type: voidptr_type ('*')+ (alt 3/3): void* followed by one or more stars -> void**
voidptr_type: 'void' '*' — two tokens; in void** the voidptr_type is the first void* only
pointer_indirection_expression: '*' unary_expression -> `*p`
